body.x: Olympus Korea showcased its “M.ZUIKO DIGITAL ED 300mm F4.0 IS PRO”, a high-performance, super-telephoto lens, and the outdoor camera “TG-870” at “CES (Consumer Electronic Show) 2016”, the world’s largest IT electronics and tech exhibition, which runs for four days from Wednesday the 6th to Saturday the 9th in Las Vegas.

The “M.ZUIKO DIGITAL ED 300mm F4.0 IS PRO”, the world’s first super-telephoto lens with six stops of stabilization, is a high-performance, super-telephoto Micro Four Thirds lens with 35mm equivalent focal length of 600mm. The product features a built-in 5-Axis Sync Image Stabilization technology and six shutter speed steps of stabilization.
The 5-Axis Sync Image Stabilization technology, which the company newly developed, maximizes its effect by interworking with the stabilization function, applied to the lens and the body.

With its four shutter speed steps for stabilization, it can also work in conjunction with the OM-D E-M1 and E-M5 Mark II bodies, which possess the 5-Axis Sync Image Stabilization function to offer six steps of stabilization.

Furthermore, it is very small with a maximum diameter of 92.5mm, and it is easy to carry, as it weighs only 1,475g (with a tripod adapter). One should consider that it is a high-performance, super-telephoto lens with a 35mm equivalent focal length of 600mm.
It enables users to capture birds, wildlife subjects, landscapes, and sports actions with high accuracy. This can be achieved without using a tripod, even in the extreme telephoto shooting mode.

Furthermore, it produces the best image quality among Olympus’ ZUIKO lenses, with high-speed AF, splash-, dust-, and freeze-proof functions, and special optical lenses including super ED, HR, and E-HR lenses. By using the new “Z Coating Nano” technology, it significantly reduces lens flare and ghosting, and produces much clearer images.
The company also showcased its “STYLUS TG-870 (hereafter TG-870)”, an outdoor camera with 180-degree tilting LCD.

Equipped with the tilting LCD for the first time for waterproof cameras, the TG-870 possesses an ultra-wide-angle 21mm lens with 5x optical zoom, a 16-megapixel image processing engine, GPS, and a Wi-Fi function, which are the advantages of its predecessor.

It also has new art filters and an advanced LCD monitor. In particular, the monitor is 920,000-pixel high-resolution, and its boost function can increase brightness by up to 2.6 times for viewing in bright light. This enables users to see objects in more detail in bright areas and capture photos more effectively. It also has an “Autofocus-Lock” function, which corrects distortions on ultra-wide group selfie shots. With a small USB charger, it is highly portable.

The TG-870 is built to withstand extreme conditions. The camera is waterproof up to depths of 50 feet (15m), freeze-proof up to -10°C, shock-proof from 2.1m high, crush-proof up to 100 kg of force, and dustproof.
This product can be used in various environments, including beaches, ski resorts, and for rock climbing, where users could shoot quality photographs by using existing cameras.
The two products will be launched domestically in February. The price is yet to be determined.

Jeong Hoon, the director of the imaging business division at Olympus, said: “The 300mm PRO lens opens up a new chapter of super-telephoto shooting, all through high portability, outstanding optical performance, and the world’s best stabilization technology. The TG-870 is receiving attention as a must-have item for ski resorts. Those two products, created by Olympus’ excellent optical technology, are expected to provide new pleasures to photography.”

Held annually in January and owned and produced by the Consumer Technology Association (CTA), CES 2016 is the world's largest exhibition to see the latest global trends in electronics and IT industry in one spot.

AVING News has been sending its reporters to CES for 11 years to introduce the new technologies and products. After the local coverage and research, AVING News will hold 'CES 2016 Review Conference' in AVING Studio, Korea on January 28th.
